title: ZFS pools are unavailable
status: unreviewed: first estimates by Claude on 2026-11-04, not yet reviewed by the author

causes.title: Running kernel is newer than zfs-dkms supports
causes.why: On Arch the kernel moves faster than OpenZFS; after a kernel upgrade this is the classic way the module goes missing.

causes.title: Kernel headers missing or not matching the running kernel
causes.why: dkms builds against linux-headers; a partial upgrade or a missing headers package stops the build.

causes.title: dkms build failed for another reason
causes.why: Compiler or toolchain changes, a broken zfs-dkms package, a full /var.

causes.title: Pool import units disabled or not run
causes.why: The module is fine but zfs-import-cache/zfs-import-scan never ran, so no pool is imported.

causes.title: Pool or disk fault
causes.why: A faulted vdev or a dead disk; rarer than the packaging causes on a box that was simply switched off.

evidence.title: Running kernel is above zfs-dkms Linux-Maximum
evidence.why: The META file says this kernel is outside the supported range: very likely under kernel-unsupported, rare otherwise (only if META were wrong).

evidence.title: linux-headers matches the running kernel
evidence.why: Matching headers make a headers problem very unlikely.

evidence.title: linux-headers does not match the running kernel
evidence.why: Mismatched headers are exactly what this cause predicts.

evidence.title: No zfs module exists for the running kernel
evidence.why: A missing module points at the build, not at import units or the pool, which need the module to even be checked.

evidence.title: dkms has zfs registered but not built
evidence.why: "added" without "installed" means the build never succeeded: favours the three build causes equally.

evidence.title: zfs-import-cache.service is enabled
evidence.why: Enabled import units make the disabled-import cause unlikely (they could still fail to run).

evidence.title: The AUR has a newer zfs-dkms
evidence.why: Weak: newer releases usually extend kernel support, which fits a kernel that outran the installed one.

evidence.title: A libvirt storage pool is inactive
evidence.why: A downstream symptom: it confirms ZFS is unavailable but does not tell causes apart, so it moves nothing.
